basis: CSX’s April 16 earnings release was the earliest verified qualifying communication. Its consolidated income statement reports $3,423 million of revenue for the quarter ended March 31, 2025 against $3,681 million a year earlier. That puts reported revenue $73.95 million below the $3,496.95 million cutoff. Both figures come from the same GAAP table. The prior-period accounting revision concerned operating expense and the balance sheet. The recovered February 19 conference transcript closes the prior review’s gap: management gave an annual headwind estimate and a quarterly coal-yield forecast, but no numeric upper bound for consolidated Q1 revenue.

coverage.detail: October 16, preceding earnings cycle. CSX expected a moderate Q4 2024 revenue decline and about $200 million of pressure from fuel and coal markets. The forecast covered the December quarter.
November 7 Investor Day. The revenue target was mid-single-digit compound annual growth from 2024 to 2027. It supplied no quarterly endpoint.
November 13 Baird remarks. Pelkey discussed the three-year earnings outlook and identified domestic coal and network pressures for 2025 without quantifying consolidated Q1 revenue.
November 19 Stephens remarks. Asked about the first quarter, management deferred the 2025 outlook to January and discussed the duration of Blue Ridge rerouting.
December 4 UBS remarks. Management discussed 2025 network disruption, commodity prices and multi-year growth targets. It gave no consolidated Q1 revenue ceiling.
January 23, previous earnings release. The $3.54 billion revenue and 4% year-over-year decline were Q4 2024 actuals. The release gave no numeric Q1 2025 revenue outlook.
January 23 presentation, slide 18. The low- to mid-single-digit growth outlook covered full-year volume. Management described coal, diesel and mix pressures on revenue, especially in the first half.

January 23 call. The roughly 3% sequential Q1 decline applied to coal revenue per unit. The $350 million headwind discussed in Q&A included disruption costs. Neither figure establishes consolidated Q1 sales.
January 27 Exhibit 99.1 announced Ann Begeman’s board appointment.
CSX’s February 11 notice identifies the February 19 Barclays session, 8:40 a.m. Eastern, with CEO Joe Hinrichs and CFO Sean Pelkey. It announced a live webcast and replay.
The issuer archive search surfaced the 2026 Barclays session. The 2025 year-filter request did not return a readable replay.
The conference-host search returned a Barclays agenda listing CSX, but the document itself dates the meeting to February 2022. It cannot establish the 2025 remarks.

The public excerpt identifies the speakers and reaches the moderator’s opening profitability question. A second transcript preview also stops at the introduction. [Zonebourse preview](https://www.zonebourse.com/cours/action/CSX-CORPORATION-25500636/actualite/Transcript-CSX-Corporation-Presents-at-Barclays-42nd-Annual-Industrial-Select-Conference-2025-Feb-49102183/)

February 19 gap resolved. A second web retrieval returned the speaker-by-speaker transcript through the moderator’s closing thanks. Asked directly about Q1 guidance, Pelkey put the approximately $350 million headwind over the full year, including rerouting costs, and described Q1 as the likely earnings trough. He separately confirmed a 3% sequential decline in coal yield. The session gave no numeric upper bound for consolidated Q1 revenue.

March 7 Form 8-K disclosed the underwriting agreement for $600 million of notes due 2035. The March 10 filing confirmed the financing closed. [March 10 Form 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/277948/000119312525050848/d940299d8k.htm)

March 11 J.P. Morgan conference. The eight-page issuer deck compares January and February daily freight volumes with Q4 averages. In Q&A, Pelkey retained full-year volume guidance and identified roughly $10 million per month of disruption costs within the $350 million headwind. He gave no Q1 consolidated revenue endpoint. [Conference transcript](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/csx/transcripts/325470-j-p-morgan-industrials-conference-2025/)
March 19 notice scheduled results for after market close on April 16. It contained no preliminary revenue figure.
April 16 Exhibit 99.2, consolidated income statement, dollars in millions. The revenue row shows 3,423 for Q1 2025 and 3,681 for Q1 2024, a reported 7% decline.

publication_date_evidence: CSX datelined its first-quarter results April 16, 2025. EDGAR accepted the Item 2.02 Form 8-K containing the release and comparative statements that day at 16:01:28.
